Then add checks for the Code review findings on the coverage gate that a developer can see, and play the walkthrough drive last.

Walkthrough D-1 played once on the head; its report and video sent.
remaining: The QA person reviews the run at the Test run gate.
decisions: Low, confirmed, high confidence: with git diff output that has no a/ and b/ prefixes, as diff.noprefix gives, scripts/coverage-patch.mjs scores a changed line that no test runs as 100 percent and passes the gate. Who notices: a developer running the script locally with that git setting. What they see: a false pass. Not on CI's path, where git's default prefixes apply. Proved by TC-8 against the control TC-7, and read in the code at line 29. Code review's open finding, outside AC-1.

Medium, confirmed in code, medium confidence: the CI test job checks out the pull request's merge commit, while coverage-patch diffs base...head, so the coverage line numbers can belong to a different tree than the changed-line numbers. Who notices: a pull request author when main has changed lines above theirs in the same file. What they see: the coverage gate passes or fails on the wrong lines. Confirmed by reading .github/workflows/ci.yml: the test job's checkout has no ref. Not run: it needs a GitHub pull request event. Code review's open finding, outside AC-1.

Low, confirmed in code: the workflow pins actions by mutable tags while the coverage-patch job holds statuses: write. No check was added: it is a configuration audit with no running consequence. Code review's open finding.

Environment, explained away, not a defect: Playwright's request fixture cannot reach the QA host because it ignores the environment's HTTPS proxy and connects directly (ETIMEDOUT). The browser uses the proxy, so the tests read the served page from the browser's response to page.goto.

The coverage tests that run commands (TC-1, TC-2, TC-3) build and test the repository at the tested commit in the work folder and check the result in the QA app. TC-1 ties the two by the bundle's content hash.
uncertain: Whether Code review's merge-ref finding (medium) should be fixed in this Deliverable: it lies outside AC-1, and only a GitHub pull request run can show it. The QA person decides.
TC-7 and TC-8 are stubbed (a fake git prints the diff), so they prove the script's parsing, not git itself. They count for no criterion.
The run id was not in the brief or the environment, so the report gives the brief's id as run_id. Ada's record of the run settles it.

Playwright wrote its results folder, with the walkthrough video, to test-results/ at the repository root, outside out/: the brief's config sets no outputDir. The folder is in .gitignore, so it is never committed.
handoff.note: AC-1 is met by TC-1 to TC-6, all passing on the head at 7d083fbbf227acf6956b0cd68105f46d2e086b1b. No defect was found. The three Code review findings concern the CI coverage gate, which AC-1 does not cover; they stay open as findings.

suggested_follow_ups: In scripts/coverage-patch.mjs, pass --src-prefix=a/ --dst-prefix=b/ (or --no-prefix and parse accordingly) to git diff, so local git settings cannot make the gate report 100 percent.
In .github/workflows/ci.yml, check out github.event.pull_request.head.sha in the test job, or diff against the merge commit, so the lcov lines and the changed lines come from the same tree.
Pin the workflow's actions to full commit SHAs.
